overview: Papua New Guinea covers the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and many smaller islands. Its capital and largest city is Port Moresby. It became independent from Australia in 1975. Papua New Guinea is one of the most culturally diverse countries in the world: more than 800 languages are spoken there.

geography.text: A high mountain range runs along the centre of the mainland, with valleys where many people live in small farming communities. Much of the country is covered by tropical rainforest, some of the largest areas of rainforest left in the world. It lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has active volcanoes, and its many islands include New Britain and Bougainville.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical and humid, cooler in the highlands.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Birds of paradise and tree kangaroos.

history.text: People have lived in New Guinea for at least 40,000 years, and its highlands were one of the first places in the world where farming developed. In the 1880s the north was claimed by Germany and the south by Britain, which later handed it to Australia. Papua New Guinea became independent from Australia in 1975.

events.title: Colonial claims
events.text: Germany claims the north-east and Britain the south-east.

events.title: Australian rule
events.text: Australia takes over the south, called Papua.

events.title: Kokoda Track
events.text: Australian troops fight Japanese forces in the mountains.

events.title: Bougainville peace deal
events.text: An agreement ends years of conflict on Bougainville.

government.text: Papua New Guinea is a constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth. The British monarch is head of state, represented by a Governor-General, and the Prime Minister leads the government. Bougainville voted for independence in a 2019 referendum, and talks on its future continue.

economy.text: Papua New Guinea is rich in natural resources: gold, copper, oil and liquefied natural gas. But most people live by farming in rural villages, growing their own food. Coffee, cocoa and palm oil are important exports.

culture.text: Papua New Guinea is the most linguistically diverse country in the world, with more than 800 languages. Tok Pisin is the most widely used. Its highlands hold colourful 'sing-sing' gatherings where groups perform in feathers and body paint.

items.title: 800 languages
items.text: More languages than any other country.

items.title: Sing-sing
items.text: Festivals of dance, song and traditional dress.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Mumu, food cooked in an earth oven.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Carvings from the Sepik River and bilum string bags.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Highland sing-sing festivals bring together hundreds of groups.

sport.text: Rugby league is the national sport and a passion across the country. Papua New Guinea joins Australia's top rugby league competition with its own team in 2028.

items.text: A Papua New Guinea team will join Australia's NRL.
